back:
Single quotes: a character value. Only one symbol, e.g. 'H'.
Double quotes: a text value. Zero or more characters, e.g. "Hello" or "H".
No quotes: a numeric value, e.g. 5 or -6.7.

If a character or text value is not quoted, the compiler treats it as code and you almost always get a compile error.
front: How do single quotes, double quotes, and no quotes change how the compiler reads a value?
